transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Yeah, um, well my supervisor basically told me I needed to come talk to someone. What brought me in is I just... I keep leaving my station on the floor. I work in production, mostly packing the smaller parts, which honestly gets so mind-numbing. Like, you wouldn't believe how many little plastic caps go into a single box. My friend Sarah used to work on the line with me, but she quit last month to work at this bakery downtown. That sounds way better, honestly, because at least it smells like bread all day instead of hot plastic and grease. Have you ever been to that bakery on 4th street? They have these amazing blueberry muffins that are like, the size of your head... 

Wait, what was I saying? Oh, right, my job. Yeah, so I keep leaving my station, and I'll even pop up and walk around during our shift meetings when I'm supposed to just stay put in my chair. My supervisor is getting really mad and says it's becoming a huge safety problem because I just take off before I even think about it. So... yeah, here I am.
Do you think before you get up and leave your station, or does it happen without you thinking about it first?

No, exactly, that's the thing—I don't think about it at all. Like I was just saying, I just take off before the thought even crosses my mind. I'm supposed to stay put, especially during those shift meetings, but I'll just pop up out of nowhere. My legs just kind of do it on their own, which is why my supervisor says it's such a huge safety problem. 

He's obsessed with safety, honestly. He wears his heavy-duty safety glasses even when he's just microwaving his lunch in the breakroom. Have you ever tried eating hot soup with safety glasses on? They fog up completely, it looks so funny. But yeah, there's a lot of moving machinery on the production floor, so he gets really mad. Like last Tuesday, I ended up all the way over by the loading docks without even realizing I'd left my chair, just because I saw them wheeling in a new vending machine. I really hope they put Funyuns in this one. The old machine only had those weird baked potato chips that taste like cardboard, and if you're working a ten-hour shift, you need actual snacks, you know? But yeah, I don't plan to get up, it just happens.
Do you find it hard to focus on a single task for a long time?

Yeah, definitely. It's like... okay, so when I'm doing the inventory logs, or they make us read those CNC training pages, I really, really try to pay attention. I start out strong, but then after just a few minutes, all the numbers and words just kind of blur together. I end up having to go back and re-read the same paragraph like five times because I didn't take any of it in. 

It's kind of like when you're watching a movie and you realize you haven't been paying attention for the last twenty minutes. My boyfriend does that all the time when we watch Marvel movies. He'll just start scrolling on his phone, and then he's like, "Wait, who is that guy?" And I'm like, "Babe, they literally just explained his whole backstory!" We went to see the new Spider-Man last weekend and we got those huge slushies. Mine was cherry and his was blue raspberry, but they gave us those paper straws and it got totally soggy before the previews were even over. I hate paper straws so much, they just dissolve in your mouth. 

But yeah, the training pages. I just can't focus on them for very long at all.
Do you often act on impulse in situations outside of work?

Outside of work? Um... I'm not really sure. I haven't really noticed if I do. I mean, when I'm not at the plant I mostly just hang out with my boyfriend or go to the mall with my sister. We actually went to the mall this past weekend because she needed a dress for her friend's wedding. It's an outdoor wedding, which is just a terrible idea right now because it's been raining so much. Why do people plan outdoor weddings in the spring? You just know it's gonna pour and ruin everyone's shoes. 

We ended up sitting in the food court for like two hours instead of shopping because they just opened this new pretzel stand. Have you ever had those little pretzel bites with the cinnamon sugar on them? They are so good, but the sugar gets literally everywhere. My car seats are still completely covered in it. I have an older Honda and the seats are that dark black fabric, so every single crumb shows up. I really need to take it to the car wash and use those giant vacuums they have out front. The ones at the gas station by my house are always broken, or they have zero suction, so it's basically pointless... 

Wait, what were we talking about? Oh, right, acting on impulse. Yeah, I don't really know, I haven't really noticed anything like that.
Do you have trouble keeping your workspace or living space organized?

Um... I don't think so? I mean, I don't really know if I have trouble with it. My workspace at the plant is pretty much just my chair and the control panel, so there's not a lot to organize, really. But my apartment... I guess it's fine? I share it with my boyfriend, and we kind of just leave things wherever. 

Actually, speaking of our apartment, our landlord just sent us this letter saying they're increasing the rent next month, which is so annoying because they haven't even fixed the leak under the kitchen sink. It's been dripping for like three weeks. We have to keep this ugly plastic bucket under it, and you have to empty it every couple of days or it spills over onto the linoleum. The linoleum is that really gross 70s orange color anyway, so it's not like water is gonna ruin it, but still. My boyfriend tried to fix it himself with duct tape, but obviously that didn't work. He thinks he's so handy because he watches those DIY videos on YouTube, but he always just makes it worse. Like the time he tried to install a dimmer switch in the bathroom and we didn't have lights in there for a week. We had to shower in the dark, which is actually kind of terrifying because I'm always convinced there's a spider in the tub. 

But yeah, organizing... I don't really know if I have trouble with it, I just kind of live how I live.
Do you have trouble paying attention or following instructions when you're with your friends or family, outside of work or school?

With my friends or family? Um, I don't really think so. I mean, we usually just hang out, so there aren't really instructions to follow or anything. Like, my sister and I were just at our mom's house for Sunday dinner. Mom made this huge pot roast with potatoes and carrots, which is honestly so annoying of her because she knows my sister is trying to do that keto diet thing. Have you heard of that? It sounds completely miserable. You basically can't eat bread or potatoes ever again. I could never give up bread. 

Have you ever had those Texas Roadhouse rolls with the cinnamon butter? They are literally the best thing on the planet. We went there for my 21st birthday a few months ago and I think I ate like six of them before my food even came out. My boyfriend got so mad because I was way too full to eat my actual meal, and he had to pay for it. But honestly, steak is so overpriced at restaurants anyway. Like, you're paying thirty dollars for a piece of meat you could buy at Food Lion for ten bucks and just cook yourself. We don't have a grill at our apartment though, because of fire codes or whatever. The leasing office lady is so incredibly strict about it. She literally walks around the parking lot on weekends with a clipboard just looking for people breaking the rules... 

Wait, what did you ask me? Something about my mom's house?
Do you often interrupt others when they're speaking, like when you're talking with your boyfriend or sister?

Yeah, I guess I do that. Like, I cut in on people without really meaning to. I do it at work a lot, actually. I'll just jump right into my coworkers' conversations, or like, I'll answer a question before the shift lead is even done talking. And then everybody gets so irritated with me. 

But honestly, the lead—his name is Gary—he talks so slow. And he's always in a bad mood anyway. He drinks like four cans of those green Monster energy drinks before our lunch break. I don't know how his heart hasn't just exploded. My boyfriend used to drink those when he worked the night shift, but it totally messed up his stomach, so he bought this fancy espresso machine off Facebook Marketplace instead. The guy who sold it to him said it was in brand new condition, but the little milk frother wand is completely clogged up. We tried soaking it in white vinegar because this girl on TikTok said it breaks down the calcium buildup. Her whole page is just cleaning stuff, which is weirdly relaxing to watch. She has this massive fluffy dog that just lays on the living room rug while she vacuums around him... 

Wait, what were we talking about? Did you ask about my boyfriend?
Do you often feel like you're fidgeting or have excess energy when you're not at work?

Well, outside of work, maybe? But honestly, it's the worst when they make me sit still for things. Like, if I have to sit for the certification class or a safety meeting at the plant, my foot is just constantly bouncing. I'm always clicking a pen, picking at my sleeves, or shifting around in my chair so much that people literally ask me to stop. 

The guy who runs the safety meetings, Don, he gets so mad at me. He always wears this ridiculous neon orange safety vest, even when he's just sitting in the conference room, which makes absolutely no sense. I actually bought a sweater that exact same neon orange color last year because I went to this outdoor music festival with my friend Chloe, and we wanted to make sure we didn't lose each other in the crowd. But then it ended up raining the entire weekend and the whole place turned into a giant mud pit. Chloe completely ruined her favorite pair of white Converse. I told her not to wear white shoes to a festival, but she never listens. She bought them on Poshmark anyway, so they were already kind of beat up. I love Poshmark, honestly. I just sold a bunch of old clothes on there, but the shipping fees are getting absolutely ridiculous. Plus, the post office by my apartment always has a line out the door, and the lady who works at the counter takes like ten minutes per person. 

Wait, what did you ask me? Something about the safety meetings?
Do you often make noise or create a commotion when you're doing things, even when you're trying to be quiet?

Yeah, I really can't do the quiet thing. It honestly makes me feel totally trapped. Like, if I try to just sit in the break room at work and read the new safety manual or whatever, I can't just be quiet. I end up humming, or tapping on the table, or I'll just start talking to whoever else is in there. Or I just have to get up and leave. 

I was in the break room yesterday and this girl Sarah was in there eating a tuna sandwich, which is honestly so gross to bring to work. The whole room smelled like fish for the rest of the day. And she was watching a video on her phone without headphones, which I think is so rude. Like, nobody wants to hear your TikToks. But it was some makeup tutorial, and the girl in the video was using this crazy bright blue eyeliner. I used to wear blue eyeliner in middle school, but I stopped because my older sister told me it made me look like a clown. My sister is so mean sometimes. She's getting married next year and she wants all the bridesmaids to wear these hideous pastel green dresses. I look terrible in green. It washes me out completely. I tried telling her we should do navy blue instead, but she's completely obsessed with this "enchanted forest" theme she saw on Pinterest. She's already bought like fifty fake moss centerpieces for the tables...

Wait, what did you ask me? Something about the break room?
Do you have trouble waiting for your turn in lines or when doing things with others?

Lines? I mean, I don't really know, I don't really pay attention to that. I guess I don't wait in lines much? Like, if there's a line at the gas station, I just leave. I don't have time for that. I'm always running late anyway. 

My car has this terrible habit of not starting on the first try, so I'm always rushing. It's a Honda Civic, but it's like twenty years old. The guy who sold it to me said it just needed a new battery, but I've replaced it twice and it still does it. My boyfriend says it's the alternator, but he's not a mechanic, he just watches a lot of YouTube videos about cars. He actually tried to fix his mom's sink last week after watching a video, and he ended up flooding her entire kitchen. She was so mad. She had just put down this really nice laminate flooring that looks like real hardwood. It's crazy how real they make that stuff look now. I went to Home Depot with them to pick it out, and the guy working in that section was so helpful. He had this really cool tattoo of a compass on his forearm. I've been thinking about getting a tattoo, but I can't decide what I want. Maybe a butterfly? Or like, a little moon on my wrist? Chloe said she'd go with me if I do it, but she has a really low pain tolerance...

Wait, sorry, what were we talking about? Did you ask about my car?
Do you often find yourself losing your temper or getting really upset over small things?

Losing my temper? I mean, I wouldn't say I get really upset over small things. Like, I don't think I do? Maybe I get a little annoyed sometimes, but who doesn't, right? 

Like, the other day, I was at the grocery store, and they completely rearranged the cereal aisle. Why do they do that? You finally figure out where everything is, and then bam, the Frosted Flakes are suddenly next to the oatmeal. I was looking for the store-brand cinnamon squares because they taste exactly the same as Cinnamon Toast Crunch but they're like two dollars cheaper. Groceries are so expensive right now. I bought a carton of eggs last week and it was almost six bucks! It's ridiculous. My grandma used to have chickens in her backyard when I was a kid, and we'd get fresh eggs every morning. She lived out in the country, and she had this huge garden where she grew her own tomatoes. They were the best tomatoes I've ever had. You just can't get tomatoes like that at the store anymore, they're all watery and gross. I tried to grow a tomato plant on my balcony last summer, but I kept forgetting to water it and it just completely died. I'm terrible with plants. My friend Chloe has a whole apartment full of succulents, and she says they're impossible to kill, but I bet I could find a way... 

Wait, what did you ask me? Something about the grocery store?
Do you often blurt out answers or interrupt others when you're in a group or talking with friends?

Yeah, I do that a lot actually. I cut in on people without even meaning to. Like on the floor, I'll just jump right into my coworkers' conversations out of nowhere, or I'll answer a question before the line lead is even done talking, and then everybody gets so irritated with me. 

But our lead, Marcus, he takes his job way too seriously anyway. He walks around with this clipboard like he's the CEO, but we're literally just packing boxes of dog toys. Some of them are really cute, though. There's this one that looks like a little plush taco, and it has two squeakers in it. I almost bought one for my neighbor's dog. My neighbor has this tiny little Chihuahua mix named Peanut, and he barks at absolutely everything. A leaf blows across the sidewalk, he barks. It's so annoying because the walls in my apartment building are like paper. I can hear the guy upstairs walking around at 3 AM every single night. It sounds like he's bowling up there or moving furniture. I really want to move, but saving up for a security deposit is impossible right now. I was looking at this one place online and they wanted first month, last month, and a deposit. Who has that kind of money just sitting around? Jessica said she found a place with no deposit, but it's way out by the highway, and I don't want to commute that far... 

Wait, sorry. What were we talking about? Did you ask about my line lead?
Do you often find yourself getting really angry or frustrated for no good reason?

Angry for no reason? Um, no, I don't think so. Like, if I get mad, there's usually a reason, you know? It's not just out of nowhere. I mean, sometimes I get frustrated, but it's usually because something is actually annoying. 

Like my phone charger. I swear it only works if I hold the cord at this very specific, weird angle, and if I let go, it stops charging. It's so frustrating. I need to just buy a new one, but every time I go to Target, I completely forget. Target is dangerous anyway, I always walk in for one thing and leave with a cart full of stuff I don't need. Last time I went for toothpaste and ended up buying this giant fuzzy throw blanket. It's so soft, though, like sleeping under a cloud. My cat, Luna, is obsessed with it. She makes biscuits on it for like twenty minutes before she finally settles down. She's a rescue, I found her behind a dumpster when she was a tiny kitten. She had this awful eye infection, but the vet got it cleared right up. Vets are so expensive, though. I had to put the bill on my credit card, which I'm trying to pay down, but the interest rate is insane. I keep getting those offers in the mail to transfer my balance, but they all have hidden fees, and I don't really understand how they work. My friend Jessica used one of those and she said it messed up her credit score for like a year...

Wait, sorry. Did you ask me about my cat? What was the question?
Do you often find yourself unable to finish tasks or projects that you start?

Finish tasks? I mean, I don't really know if I have a problem with that. Like, I don't think I leave things unfinished on purpose, you know? I usually try to get things done when I start them. 

Like, I started painting my bedroom last month. Well, I started taping off the baseboards, anyway. I got this really pretty color, it's called "Seafoam Whisper," and it looks exactly like the ocean when it's cloudy. I love the ocean. My mom took me to the beach when I was like ten, and we collected all these tiny seashells. I kept them in a glass jar on my dresser for years until my brother accidentally knocked it over and it shattered everywhere. He was always breaking my stuff. He broke my favorite CD player once because he tried to shove a piece of toast into the disc drive. Who does that? He was obsessed with toast for a while, he'd eat it with just butter, no jam, nothing. I hate plain toast, it's so dry. You need something on it, like peanut butter or avocado. Avocado toast is so good, but avocados go bad so fast. You buy them and they're hard as a rock, and then you blink and they're complete mush. I tried putting them in the fridge to make them last longer, but I always forget they're in the crisper drawer until they're totally rotten. The crisper drawer is basically just a graveyard for vegetables in my apartment. I bought a bag of spinach like three weeks ago and I'm pretty sure it's turned into actual liquid by now. I really need to clean out my fridge, it smells kind of weird...

Wait, what were you asking me? Something about my bedroom?
Do you have trouble paying attention in class or when doing homework, if you're in school, or in other situations where you need to focus?

Yeah, focusing is really hard for me. Like at work, when I'm doing the inventory logs or trying to read through those CNC training pages they gave us, I start out really trying. I sit down, I tell myself I'm going to get through it, but after a few minutes, the numbers and words just start blurring together. I have to keep going back and re-reading the same page over and over because I didn't take any of it in. 

It's like my brain just switches off. Or, well, not off, but it switches to something else. Like yesterday I was trying to read the manual and I started thinking about how weird the font was. It was like this super blocky text, kind of like the font they use on those old arcade games. I loved going to the arcade when I was little. There was this one by my old house that had a giant Pac-Man machine, like the screen was the size of a wall. I spent so many quarters on that thing. My grandpa used to give me a roll of quarters every time he visited, and he always smelled like peppermints and old leather. He drove this huge boat of a car, a Lincoln Town Car, I think? It was light blue and the seats were so squishy, like sitting on a marshmallow. I miss cars having bench seats in the front. Now everything has that middle console thing, which is nice for holding drinks, I guess. I bought this huge insulated cup the other day because I'm trying to drink more water, but it doesn't fit in my car's cup holder. It just tips over every time I turn a corner, which is super annoying. I spilled ice water all over my passenger seat on Tuesday, and it took forever to dry. It left this weird water stain, too. I tried scrubbing it with some upholstery cleaner I found under my sink, but it smells really strongly of fake lemons. Like, chemically lemons, you know? 

Wait, what was the question? Did you ask about my car?
Do you often feel overwhelmed by your emotions and have trouble calming down?

Overwhelmed by my emotions? Um, I don't really think so. I mean, I get upset sometimes, but I don't think it's, like, out of control or anything. I can usually calm down okay if I just take a minute. 

Like when I get stressed, I just need a distraction, you know? So I usually try to listen to music. I have this one playlist I made that's just, like, 90s alternative stuff. It's so good. Nirvana, Pearl Jam, Smashing Pumpkins. I actually found this vintage Smashing Pumpkins t-shirt at a thrift store last weekend. It was in the men's section, which is where you always find the best vintage shirts, honestly. The women's section is always full of, like, weird blouses with shoulder pads. Why did people ever think shoulder pads were a good idea? It just makes everyone look like a football player. My cousin played football in high school, he was a linebacker, I think. He got this really bad concussion once during a game and had to stay in a dark room for a week. He couldn't even look at his phone. I can't imagine not looking at my phone for a whole week. I'd go crazy. I play this puzzle game on my phone constantly, it's like matching different colored gems, and it's so addictive. I stayed up until 3 AM playing it the other night because I was stuck on level 400. Level 400! The levels get so ridiculously hard, they add these little ice blocks you have to break through, and if you don't do it in enough moves, you lose a life. You only get five lives, and then you have to wait like half an hour for them to regenerate. Or you can pay real money to get more, which is such a scam. I refuse to pay for mobile games. There are so many subscriptions for everything now, it's exhausting. Netflix, Hulu, Spotify, it all adds up so fast...

Wait, sorry. What were you asking me? Did you ask about my music?
Do you often find it hard to keep your mind on one thing for an extended period of time?

Yeah, I mean, kind of like I was just saying before, right? About work? When I'm trying to do the inventory logs or read through those CNC training pages, it's impossible to just stick with it for very long. I start out really trying to keep my mind on it, but after a few minutes, the numbers and words just completely blur together. I realize I didn't take any of it in, so I have to keep going back and starting over. 

It's so frustrating. And those CNC machines are incredibly loud, anyway. They make us wear these squishy orange foam earplugs, but they always pop out of my ears. I think my ear canals are weirdly shaped or something. My mom used to say I had elf ears when I was a kid because they point just a little bit at the top. I actually wanted to be an elf for Halloween last year, like from Lord of the Rings, but the pointy ear prosthetics I bought online gave me a horrible rash. My skin is super sensitive. I can't even use regular laundry detergent, I have to buy the expensive stuff that's clear and doesn't have any dyes in it. But it doesn't even smell like anything! Half the point of doing laundry is making your clothes smell like fresh rain or whatever. I bought this fabric softener once that smelled like lavender and vanilla, and it was amazing, but my washing machine broke right after I bought it. The landlord took three weeks to fix it. I had to go to the laundromat down the street, and the vending machine there had a bag of chips from like 2019 in it. Who is buying five-year-old Doritos? That's just asking for food poisoning. I got food poisoning from a gas station hot dog once and I swear I thought I was going to die...

Wait, sorry, my brain just went totally off track. What were you asking me? Did you ask about my laundry?
Do you often struggle to complete tasks or achieve goals due to getting distracted or losing focus?

Goals? Um, I don't really think so. I mean, I finish my shift at the plant every day, so that's completing a task, right? And I don't really have a lot of big goals that I'm, like, failing at or anything. 

I guess my last goal was trying to learn how to roller skate. I bought these really cute vintage-looking skates online a few months ago. They were bright yellow with these chunky pink wheels. Pink is my favorite color, well, like a hot neon pink, not baby pink. Baby pink totally washes me out. I tried to dye my hair baby pink once, back in like 10th grade before I stopped going to school, and it looked terrible. It just looked like a faded, weird strawberry blonde. My friend Sarah helped me do it in her bathroom, and we accidentally stained her mom's expensive white towels. Her mom was so mad, she grounded Sarah for a whole week. Sarah's mom was super strict anyway, she used to make us eat these weird organic snacks that tasted like actual cardboard. Like flaxseed crackers or something? I love crackers, but only the bad-for-you kind. Cheez-Its are the absolute best, especially the extra toasty ones in the red box. I could eat a whole box of those in one sitting while watching TV. I've been rewatching this old reality show about people who build giant custom fish tanks for rich people. It's wild how much money people will spend just to have a fish tank shaped like a telephone booth. I used to have a goldfish when I was seven, but my cat ate it. 

Wait, sorry, I'm doing it again. What was the question? Did you ask about my fish?
Do you think your difficulties with focusing and impulsivity are equally problematic for you, or does one cause you more trouble than the other?

Focusing and impulsivity? Um, I don't know, honestly. I don't really think about it like that, like weighing them against each other or anything. I guess they both just kind of happen? 

Like, I don't sit there and think, "Oh, my focus is worse today than my impulsivity." It's just my brain doing its thing. It's kind of like how I don't really think about what I'm going to eat for lunch until I'm already in the breakroom staring at the vending machine. Speaking of the vending machine, they finally restocked the good pop tarts. The s'mores ones. For like a month, all they had were the unfrosted strawberry ones, which is basically a crime against breakfast pastries. Who even eats unfrosted pop tarts? It's just dry crust. It reminds me of this time I tried to make a pie from scratch for Thanksgiving because I watched this baking show on Netflix. The Great British Baking Show, I think? I love that show, everyone is so nice to each other. Even when their cakes collapse, they're just like, "Oh dear, well done anyway." If I dropped a cake, I'd probably cry. Anyway, my pie crust turned out like actual concrete. I think I forgot to put butter in it? Or water? I don't know. My brother tried to eat a piece and he said he thought he chipped a tooth. He's so dramatic, though. He's always complaining about something. Like last week, he was complaining that his car was making a weird noise, but it turned out he just left a half-empty water bottle rolling around under the passenger seat. I told him he needs to clean out his car more often. It smells like old gym socks in there. 

Wait, sorry. What were we talking about? Did you ask about my brother's car?
Do you think you have more trouble sitting still and being patient, or paying attention and following through on instructions?

Sitting still or paying attention? Um, I don't really know. I've never really thought about which one is worse, honestly. They both just kind of happen all the time. 

Like, waiting for things is the absolute worst, though. I had to go to the DMV last month to update my ID, and the line was literally out the door. The lady taking the pictures was moving in slow motion, I swear. And my picture turned out so bad! I was wearing this green sweater that made me look totally sick. It was like a weird split-pea soup green. I actually got it at this thrift store downtown. I love thrifting, you can find the coolest stuff if you dig enough. Last time I went, I found this vintage lamp that was shaped exactly like a giant mushroom. It was amazing, but the lightbulb burned out after like two days and I couldn't figure out how to replace it because it took this tiny, weirdly shaped bulb from like the seventies. I went to three different hardware stores looking for it. Hardware stores always smell so good, though, don't they? Like cut wood and dirt. It reminds me of my grandpa's garage. He used to build birdhouses out of scrap wood. He made this one that looked like a tiny mansion, it even had a little wraparound porch on it. We painted it bright red, but the birds never even used it. I think it was too big, or maybe the paint scared them off. 

Wait, sorry, my brain is just jumping everywhere today. What did you ask me? Did you ask about the DMV?

Hi. Yeah, um, well my supervisor basically told me I needed to come talk to someone. What brought me in is I just... I keep leaving my station on the floor. I work in production, mostly packing the smaller parts, which honestly gets so mind-numbing. Like, you wouldn't believe how many little plastic caps go into a single box. My friend Sarah used to work on the line with me, but she quit last month to work at this bakery downtown. That sounds way better, honestly, because at least it smells like bread all day instead of hot plastic and grease. Have you ever been to that bakery on 4th street? They have these amazing blueberry muffins that are like, the size of your head... 

Wait, what was I saying? Oh, right, my job. Yeah, so I keep leaving my station, and I'll even pop up and walk around during our shift meetings when I'm supposed to just stay put in my chair. My supervisor is getting really mad and says it's becoming a huge safety problem because I just take off before I even think about it. So... yeah, here I am.

doctor.intent: determine if the patient's behavior is impulsive
doctor.question: Do you think before you get up and leave your station, or does it happen without you thinking about it first?

target_item.name: Leaving_Seat
target_item.manifestation: What brought me in is I keep leaving my station or popping up during meetings when I'm supposed to stay put, and my supervisor says it's becoming a safety problem because I just take off before I even think about it.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking for clarification about my chief complaint (leaving my station/seat), specifically whether I think before doing it or if it happens impulsively, which maps to S011.

patient.answer:

I love that show, everyone is so nice to each other. Even when their cakes collapse, they're just like, "Oh dear, well done anyway." If I dropped a cake, I'd probably cry. Anyway, my pie crust turned out like actual concrete. I think I forgot to put butter in it? Or water? I don't know. My brother tried to eat a piece and he said he thought he chipped a tooth. He's so dramatic, though. He's always complaining about something. Like last week, he was complaining that his car was making a weird noise, but it turned out he just left a half-empty water bottle rolling around under the passenger seat. I told him he needs to clean out his car more often. It smells like old gym socks in there. 

Wait, sorry. What were we talking about? Did you ask about my brother's car?

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient's symptoms are primarily related to inattention or hyperactivity-impulsivity
doctor.question: Do you think you have more trouble sitting still and being patient, or paying attention and following through on instructions?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking me to compare my hyperactive/impulsive symptoms with my inattentive symptoms to determine my predominant presentation type, which is not covered by any specific symptom in my profile.

patient.answer:
Sitting still or paying attention? Um, I don't really know. I've never really thought about which one is worse, honestly. They both just kind of happen all the time. 

Like, waiting for things is the absolute worst, though. I had to go to the DMV last month to update my ID, and the line was literally out the door. The lady taking the pictures was moving in slow motion, I swear. And my picture turned out so bad! I was wearing this green sweater that made me look totally sick. It was like a weird split-pea soup green. I actually got it at this thrift store downtown. I love thrifting, you can find the coolest stuff if you dig enough. Last time I went, I found this vintage lamp that was shaped exactly like a giant mushroom. It was amazing, but the lightbulb burned out after like two days and I couldn't figure out how to replace it because it took this tiny, weirdly shaped bulb from like the seventies. I went to three different hardware stores looking for it. Hardware stores always smell so good, though, don't they? Like cut wood and dirt. It reminds me of my grandpa's garage. He used to build birdhouses out of scrap wood. He made this one that looked like a tiny mansion, it even had a little wraparound porch on it. We painted it bright red, but the birds never even used it. I think it was too big, or maybe the paint scared them off. 

Wait, sorry, my brain is just jumping everywhere today. What did you ask me? Did you ask about the DMV?

opening_question.question: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient exhibits significant symptoms of inattention and impulsivity, which have been persistent and cause significant impairment in social and occupational functioning. The symptoms include difficulty sustaining focus during tasks, frequent mind-wandering, impulsive behaviors such as interrupting others and blurting out answers, and physical restlessness.
